biggest_catch: The $395 annual fee comes straight out of the bonus: 75,000 miles (about $750 in travel value at 1 cent per mile through Capital One Travel) minus the $395 fee leaves roughly $355 of first-year net value, and only if you hit $4,000 in 3 months with spending you already planned.
catches: Claim the bonus only with spending you already planned; never buy things you don't need just to hit the $4,000 target.
The $395 annual fee reduces the bonus — first-year net math is in the biggest catch above.
Applying for the card causes a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily lower your credit score.
The purchase APR is roughly 20%+; carrying a balance for even a month or two wipes out the bonus value — pay the statement balance in full every month.
You are ineligible for the bonus if you received a Venture X new-cardmember bonus in the past 48 months (Capital One's 48-month same-product rule).
The bonus posts within two billing cycles, not immediately — keep the account open until it lands.

steps: Go to the official Capital One page https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/travel-and-miles/ and read the Venture X welcome-bonus terms (75,000 miles after $4,000 in 3 months).
Confirm you have not received a Venture X new-cardmember bonus in the past 48 months — otherwise you won't get this one.
Apply online through that official page and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Within the first 3 months from account opening, put $4,000 of purchases on the card — only spending you already planned (groceries, bills, gas). Never buy extra just to hit the target.
Pay the statement balance in full every month — at ~20%+ APR, carrying a balance erases the bonus fast.
Keep the account open and watch for the 75,000 miles to post within two billing cycles of hitting the spend.
Plan how you'll redeem the miles (Capital One Travel is the simple 1-cent-per-mile baseline) before the annual fee bills again.
timing: Bonus miles post within two billing cycles after you meet the $4,000-in-3-months spend requirement.
